metadata.notes: majors/careers names+aliases+keywords are real disciplines/occupations; career growth_outlook grounded in BLS 2023-33/2024-34 projections; salary_band is an ordinal global tier (editorial); intensity/personality_fit and strength fields are editorial estimates. university_major_links strength_score>=0.80 are QS-subject-sourced (Tier A); <0.80 are institution-type inferences (Tier B).

confidence_legend.university_major_links: high = QS-subject-sourced (Tier A); low = institution-type inference (Tier B)

majors.name: Computer Science
majors.embedding_text: Computer Science is the study of programming, algorithms, software systems and artificial intelligence. It suits students who enjoy coding, logic, mathematics and solving abstract problems. Common careers include software engineer, AI engineer, data scientist and cybersecurity analyst.

majors.name: Software Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Software Engineering focuses on designing, building and maintaining large reliable software systems using disciplined engineering methods. It suits students who like building practical products and working in teams. Common careers include software engineer, DevOps engineer and systems architect.

majors.name: Data Science
majors.embedding_text: Data Science combines statistics, programming and domain knowledge to extract insight from data and build predictive models. It suits students who enjoy mathematics, coding and finding patterns. Common careers include data scientist, machine learning engineer and data analyst.

majors.name: Artificial Intelligence
majors.embedding_text: Artificial Intelligence studies how to make machines learn, reason and perceive, including neural networks, language models and robotics. It suits students strong in mathematics and programming who like research. Common careers include AI engineer, research scientist and machine learning engineer.

majors.name: Information Technology
majors.embedding_text: Information Technology focuses on deploying and managing computer systems, networks and infrastructure that organisations rely on. It suits students who like practical problem solving and working with technology. Common careers include IT administrator, network engineer and systems analyst.

majors.name: Cybersecurity
majors.embedding_text: Cybersecurity is the study of protecting computers, networks and data from attack through cryptography, secure design and threat analysis. It suits detail-oriented students who like puzzles and defense. Common careers include security analyst, penetration tester and security engineer.

majors.name: Electrical Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Electrical Engineering studies electricity, electronics, signals and power systems, from microchips to electrical grids. It suits students who enjoy physics, mathematics and building hardware. Common careers include electrical engineer, electronics engineer and power systems engineer.

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Mechanical Engineering studies forces, energy, machines and manufacturing to design physical products and systems. It suits students who like physics, mathematics and building things. Common careers include mechanical engineer, design engineer and manufacturing engineer.

majors.name: Civil Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Civil Engineering designs and builds infrastructure such as bridges, buildings, roads and water systems. It suits students who like applied physics, mathematics and large practical projects. Common careers include civil engineer, structural engineer and construction manager.

majors.name: Chemical Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Chemical Engineering applies chemistry, physics and mathematics to design processes that turn raw materials into useful products at scale. It suits students who like chemistry and problem solving. Common careers include process engineer, chemical engineer and production engineer.

majors.name: Aerospace Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Aerospace Engineering studies the design of aircraft and spacecraft, including aerodynamics, propulsion and flight systems. It suits students strong in physics and mathematics who are fascinated by flight and space. Common careers include aerospace engineer, propulsion engineer and flight systems engineer.

majors.name: Biomedical Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Biomedical Engineering applies engineering to medicine, designing devices, imaging systems and prosthetics. It suits students who like biology, physics and helping people through technology. Common careers include biomedical engineer, clinical engineer and medical device designer.

majors.name: Industrial Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Industrial Engineering improves complex systems and processes to make them more efficient, in factories, hospitals and supply chains. It suits students who like optimisation and organisation. Common careers include industrial engineer, operations analyst and supply chain engineer.

majors.name: Environmental Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Environmental Engineering uses engineering to protect the environment, treating water, controlling pollution and designing sustainable systems. It suits students who care about the planet and like applied science. Common careers include environmental engineer, water engineer and sustainability consultant.

majors.name: Materials Science
majors.embedding_text: Materials Science studies the structure and properties of materials such as metals, polymers and nanomaterials to design new substances. It suits students who like chemistry, physics and laboratory work. Common careers include materials engineer, metallurgist and research scientist.

majors.name: Mechatronics
majors.embedding_text: Mechatronics combines mechanical, electrical and software engineering to build robots and automated systems. It suits students who like building intelligent machines. Common careers include robotics engineer, automation engineer and control systems engineer.

majors.name: Mathematics
majors.embedding_text: Mathematics is the study of numbers, structures, patterns and logical proof, underpinning science and technology. It suits students who love abstract reasoning and problem solving. Common careers include data scientist, actuary, quantitative analyst and mathematician.

majors.name: Statistics
majors.embedding_text: Statistics is the science of collecting, analysing and interpreting data and quantifying uncertainty. It suits students who enjoy mathematics and reasoning about evidence. Common careers include statistician, data scientist and biostatistician.

majors.name: Physics
majors.embedding_text: Physics studies matter, energy and the fundamental laws of the universe, from particles to galaxies. It suits students who love mathematics and understanding how things work. Common careers include physicist, research scientist, data scientist and engineer.

majors.name: Chemistry
majors.embedding_text: Chemistry studies substances, their structure, properties and reactions, bridging physics and biology. It suits students who enjoy laboratory work and problem solving. Common careers include chemist, research scientist, pharmacologist and quality analyst.

majors.name: Biology
majors.embedding_text: Biology is the study of living organisms, from molecules and cells to ecosystems and evolution. It suits curious students who like science and the natural world. Common careers include biologist, research scientist, lab technician and science teacher.

majors.name: Biochemistry
majors.embedding_text: Biochemistry studies the chemical processes within living organisms, including proteins, enzymes and metabolism. It suits students who like both chemistry and biology and enjoy lab work. Common careers include biochemist, research scientist and pharmaceutical scientist.

majors.name: Biotechnology
majors.embedding_text: Biotechnology uses living systems and organisms to develop products in medicine, agriculture and industry. It suits students who like applied biology and innovation. Common careers include biotechnologist, research scientist and process scientist.

majors.name: Microbiology
majors.embedding_text: Microbiology studies microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses and fungi and their effects on health and the environment. It suits students who enjoy laboratory science. Common careers include microbiologist, clinical scientist and research scientist.

majors.name: Genetics
majors.embedding_text: Genetics studies genes, heredity and how DNA shapes living things, increasingly through genomics and big data. It suits students who like detailed biological science. Common careers include geneticist, genetic counsellor and research scientist.

majors.name: Neuroscience
majors.embedding_text: Neuroscience studies the brain and nervous system and how they produce thought, emotion and behaviour. It suits students fascinated by the mind and biology. Common careers include neuroscientist, research scientist and clinical researcher.

majors.name: Environmental Science
majors.embedding_text: Environmental Science studies the natural world and human impact on it, combining biology, chemistry and earth science. It suits students who care about sustainability. Common careers include environmental scientist, conservation officer and sustainability analyst.

majors.name: Geology
majors.embedding_text: Geology studies the Earth, its materials, structure and history, including natural resources and hazards. It suits students who like fieldwork and physical science. Common careers include geologist, geoscientist and environmental consultant.

majors.name: Astronomy
majors.embedding_text: Astronomy studies stars, planets, galaxies and the universe using physics and mathematics. It suits students who love space and abstract science. Common careers include astronomer, research scientist and data scientist.

majors.name: Medicine
majors.embedding_text: Medicine is the study and practice of diagnosing, treating and preventing illness. It suits caring, resilient students who like science and helping people. Common careers include doctor, surgeon, physician and medical researcher.

majors.name: Dentistry
majors.embedding_text: Dentistry studies oral health and the diagnosis and treatment of teeth and gums. It suits students who like hands-on clinical work and science. Common careers include dentist, orthodontist and oral surgeon.

majors.name: Pharmacy
majors.embedding_text: Pharmacy studies medicines, how they work and how they are safely used and dispensed. It suits students who like chemistry, biology and patient care. Common careers include pharmacist, clinical pharmacist and pharmaceutical scientist.

majors.name: Nursing
majors.embedding_text: Nursing is the practice of caring for patients and supporting their health and recovery. It suits compassionate, practical students who like science. Common careers include registered nurse, nurse practitioner and clinical nurse specialist.

majors.name: Public Health
majors.embedding_text: Public Health studies how to protect and improve the health of whole populations through prevention, policy and data. It suits students who like science and social impact. Common careers include public health analyst, epidemiologist and health policy advisor.

majors.name: Veterinary Science
majors.embedding_text: Veterinary Science studies the health and treatment of animals. It suits students who love animals and science and like hands-on clinical work. Common careers include veterinarian, veterinary surgeon and animal health researcher.

majors.name: Physiotherapy
majors.embedding_text: Physiotherapy helps people recover movement and manage pain after injury or illness through exercise and physical treatment. It suits practical, caring students. Common careers include physiotherapist, sports therapist and rehabilitation specialist.

majors.name: Psychology
majors.embedding_text: Psychology is the scientific study of mind and behaviour, from perception and memory to mental health. It suits students curious about people and research. Common careers include psychologist, counsellor, HR specialist and researcher.

majors.name: Economics
majors.embedding_text: Economics studies how people, businesses and governments allocate scarce resources and how markets and policy work. It suits students who like analysis and current affairs. Common careers include economist, financial analyst and policy analyst.

majors.name: Finance
majors.embedding_text: Finance studies how money, investments and markets work, including valuation, risk and corporate funding. It suits numerate, ambitious students. Common careers include financial analyst, investment banker and portfolio manager.

majors.name: Accounting
majors.embedding_text: Accounting is the recording, reporting and analysis of financial information for businesses and individuals. It suits organised, detail-oriented students. Common careers include accountant, auditor, tax advisor and financial controller.

majors.name: Business Administration
majors.embedding_text: Business Administration studies how to run and manage organisations, covering strategy, marketing, finance and operations. It suits versatile students who like leadership. Common careers include manager, consultant, analyst and entrepreneur.

majors.name: Marketing
majors.embedding_text: Marketing studies how to understand customers and promote products and brands across traditional and digital channels. It suits creative, persuasive students. Common careers include marketing manager, brand manager and digital marketer.

majors.name: International Business
majors.embedding_text: International Business studies how companies operate across borders, covering trade, strategy and cross-cultural management. It suits globally minded students. Common careers include international business manager, trade analyst and consultant.

majors.name: Entrepreneurship
majors.embedding_text: Entrepreneurship studies how to create, launch and grow new ventures and innovations. It suits independent, creative risk-takers. Common careers include founder, product manager and business developer.

majors.name: Human Resource Management
majors.embedding_text: Human Resource Management studies how to recruit, develop and support people at work. It suits people-oriented, organised students. Common careers include HR manager, talent specialist and people partner.

majors.name: Supply Chain Management
majors.embedding_text: Supply Chain Management studies how goods and services move from suppliers to customers efficiently. It suits organised, analytical students. Common careers include supply chain analyst, logistics manager and procurement specialist.

majors.name: Actuarial Science
majors.embedding_text: Actuarial Science uses mathematics, statistics and finance to measure and price risk, especially in insurance and pensions. It suits highly numerate students. Common careers include actuary, risk analyst and pricing analyst.

majors.name: Law
majors.embedding_text: Law studies the rules that govern society and how they are interpreted and applied. It suits students who like reading, argument and justice. Common careers include lawyer, solicitor, barrister and legal advisor.

majors.name: Political Science
majors.embedding_text: Political Science studies government, power, policy and political behaviour at home and abroad. It suits students who like debate and current affairs. Common careers include policy analyst, civil servant and political advisor.

majors.name: International Relations
majors.embedding_text: International Relations studies how countries and global actors interact through diplomacy, trade, security and conflict. It suits globally curious students. Common careers include diplomat, policy analyst and international affairs specialist.

majors.name: Sociology
majors.embedding_text: Sociology studies society, social behaviour and the institutions and structures that shape people's lives. It suits students interested in people and social issues. Common careers include social researcher, policy analyst and community worker.

majors.name: Anthropology
majors.embedding_text: Anthropology studies human cultures, societies and origins, often through fieldwork and ethnography. It suits curious students who like understanding people. Common careers include anthropologist, researcher and cultural consultant.

majors.name: Philosophy
majors.embedding_text: Philosophy studies fundamental questions about knowledge, reality, ethics and reasoning. It suits students who love deep thinking and argument. Common careers include researcher, writer, analyst and policy advisor.

majors.name: History
majors.embedding_text: History studies the human past through evidence and interpretation, building strong research and writing skills. It suits curious, analytical students. Common careers include historian, archivist, writer and teacher.

majors.name: Geography
majors.embedding_text: Geography studies the Earth's landscapes, environments and human populations, blending science and social science. It suits students who like maps and the world. Common careers include geographer, GIS analyst and urban planner.

majors.name: Linguistics
majors.embedding_text: Linguistics is the scientific study of language, its structure, sounds, meaning and how it is used. It suits analytical students fascinated by language. Common careers include linguist, language technologist and researcher.

majors.name: English Literature
majors.embedding_text: English Literature studies written works, their meaning, style and context, developing strong critical and writing skills. It suits keen readers and writers. Common careers include writer, editor, teacher and communications specialist.

majors.name: Journalism
majors.embedding_text: Journalism studies how to research, report and communicate news and stories accurately across media. It suits curious, articulate students. Common careers include journalist, reporter, editor and content producer.

majors.name: Communications
majors.embedding_text: Communications studies how messages are created and shared through media, public relations and strategy. It suits creative, social students. Common careers include communications manager, PR specialist and content strategist.

majors.name: Education
majors.embedding_text: Education studies how people learn and how to teach effectively across ages and subjects. It suits caring students who want to help others grow. Common careers include teacher, education advisor and instructional designer.

majors.name: Architecture
majors.embedding_text: Architecture studies the design of buildings and spaces, combining creativity, technical skill and an understanding of how people use places. It suits visual, practical students. Common careers include architect, urban designer and design consultant.

majors.name: Urban Planning
majors.embedding_text: Urban Planning studies how to design and manage towns and cities, balancing housing, transport and the environment. It suits students who like cities and policy. Common careers include urban planner, transport planner and policy analyst.

majors.name: Graphic Design
majors.embedding_text: Graphic Design studies visual communication through typography, imagery and layout for print and digital media. It suits creative, visual students. Common careers include graphic designer, UI designer and art director.

majors.name: Fine Arts
majors.embedding_text: Fine Arts studies visual creative practice such as painting, sculpture and drawing. It suits expressive, imaginative students. Common careers include artist, illustrator, curator and art teacher.

majors.name: Music
majors.embedding_text: Music studies performance, composition and theory across styles and instruments. It suits passionate, disciplined creative students. Common careers include musician, composer, music teacher and producer.

majors.name: Film and Television
majors.embedding_text: Film and Television studies how moving images are created, from screenwriting and directing to editing and production. It suits creative storytellers. Common careers include filmmaker, editor, producer and director.

majors.name: Drama and Theatre
majors.embedding_text: Drama and Theatre studies performance, acting and stagecraft. It suits expressive, collaborative students who love performing. Common careers include actor, director, drama teacher and theatre producer.

majors.name: Fashion Design
majors.embedding_text: Fashion Design studies the design and creation of clothing and accessories, combining creativity and technical skill. It suits visual, trend-aware students. Common careers include fashion designer, stylist and textile designer.

majors.name: Hospitality Management
majors.embedding_text: Hospitality Management studies how to run hotels, restaurants and tourism services with a focus on guest experience. It suits social, organised students. Common careers include hotel manager, events manager and hospitality operations lead.

majors.name: Tourism Management
majors.embedding_text: Tourism Management studies the travel and tourism industry, including destinations, services and marketing. It suits outgoing, organised students. Common careers include tourism manager, travel consultant and destination marketer.

majors.name: Culinary Arts
majors.embedding_text: Culinary Arts studies professional cooking and food preparation, blending creativity and craft. It suits hands-on, creative students who love food. Common careers include chef, food entrepreneur and food product developer.

majors.name: Agriculture
majors.embedding_text: Agriculture studies food and crop production, soil, livestock and sustainable farming. It suits practical students who like science and the outdoors. Common careers include agronomist, farm manager and agricultural scientist.

majors.name: Food Science
majors.embedding_text: Food Science studies the chemistry, processing and safety of food. It suits students who like chemistry and biology with practical application. Common careers include food scientist, quality manager and product developer.

majors.name: Forestry
majors.embedding_text: Forestry studies the management and conservation of forests and their resources. It suits outdoor-loving students who like ecology. Common careers include forester, conservation officer and environmental manager.

majors.name: Marine Biology
majors.embedding_text: Marine Biology studies life in oceans and seas and how to conserve it. It suits students fascinated by the sea and biology. Common careers include marine biologist, marine conservationist and research scientist.

majors.name: Sports Science
majors.embedding_text: Sports Science studies the body's response to exercise and how to improve performance and health. It suits active students who like biology. Common careers include sports scientist, strength coach and rehabilitation specialist.

majors.name: Nutrition and Dietetics
majors.embedding_text: Nutrition and Dietetics studies how food affects health and how to advise people on eating well. It suits caring, science-minded students. Common careers include dietitian, nutritionist and health consultant.

majors.name: Social Work
majors.embedding_text: Social Work studies how to support vulnerable people and families and connect them to help. It suits empathetic, resilient students. Common careers include social worker, case manager and community worker.

majors.name: Criminology
majors.embedding_text: Criminology studies crime, its causes and how society responds through law and justice systems. It suits students interested in society and justice. Common careers include criminologist, probation officer and policy analyst.

majors.name: Theology
majors.embedding_text: Theology and Religious Studies examine religious belief, texts, history and ethics. It suits reflective students who like reading and ideas. Common careers include researcher, chaplain, teacher and writer.

majors.name: Archaeology
majors.embedding_text: Archaeology studies human history through material remains, from excavation to analysis. It suits curious students who like history and fieldwork. Common careers include archaeologist, heritage officer and researcher.

majors.name: Pharmacology
majors.embedding_text: Pharmacology studies how drugs act on the body and how new medicines are developed and tested. It suits students who like biology and chemistry. Common careers include pharmacologist, drug researcher and clinical scientist.

majors.name: Optometry
majors.embedding_text: Optometry studies eye health and vision care, including diagnosis and correction. It suits precise, caring students who like clinical work. Common careers include optometrist, vision scientist and clinical specialist.

majors.name: Occupational Therapy
majors.embedding_text: Occupational Therapy helps people regain independence in everyday activities after injury, illness or disability. It suits practical, caring students. Common careers include occupational therapist and rehabilitation specialist.

majors.name: Speech and Language Therapy
majors.embedding_text: Speech and Language Therapy helps people with communication and swallowing difficulties. It suits patient, caring, science-minded students. Common careers include speech therapist and clinical specialist.

majors.name: Midwifery
majors.embedding_text: Midwifery studies the care of women during pregnancy, birth and beyond. It suits caring, calm and resilient students. Common careers include midwife and maternal health specialist.

majors.name: Game Development
majors.embedding_text: Game Development studies how to design and build video games, combining programming, art and design. It suits creative, technical students. Common careers include game developer, game designer and gameplay programmer.

majors.name: Information Systems
majors.embedding_text: Information Systems studies how organisations use technology and data to operate, bridging business and IT. It suits students who like both. Common careers include business analyst, systems analyst and IT consultant.

majors.name: Quantitative Finance
majors.embedding_text: Quantitative Finance applies mathematics, statistics and programming to financial markets, pricing and risk. It suits highly numerate students. Common careers include quantitative analyst, risk modeller and quantitative developer.

majors.name: Cognitive Science
majors.embedding_text: Cognitive Science studies the mind across psychology, neuroscience, linguistics and artificial intelligence. It suits interdisciplinary, curious students. Common careers include researcher, UX researcher and data scientist.

majors.name: Petroleum Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Petroleum Engineering studies the extraction of oil and gas, including drilling and reservoir management. It suits numerate students who like applied geoscience. Common careers include petroleum engineer, reservoir engineer and drilling engineer.

majors.name: Mining Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Mining Engineering studies how to extract minerals from the earth safely and efficiently. It suits practical students who like geoscience and engineering. Common careers include mining engineer, geotechnical engineer and resource analyst.

majors.name: Energy Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Energy Engineering studies how to generate, store and use energy efficiently and sustainably, including renewables. It suits students who care about energy and the climate. Common careers include energy engineer, renewable energy engineer and energy analyst.

majors.name: Telecommunications Engineering
majors.embedding_text: Telecommunications Engineering studies systems that transmit information over distance, from mobile networks to satellites. It suits students strong in physics and maths. Common careers include telecom engineer, network engineer and RF engineer.

majors.name: Bioinformatics
majors.embedding_text: Bioinformatics combines biology, computer science and statistics to analyse biological data such as genomes. It suits students who like coding and life science. Common careers include bioinformatician, computational biologist and data scientist.

majors.name: Real Estate
majors.embedding_text: Real Estate studies the property market, including valuation, development and investment. It suits commercially minded students. Common careers include surveyor, property analyst and real estate developer.

majors.name: Public Administration
majors.embedding_text: Public Administration studies how governments and public organisations are run and how policy is delivered. It suits students who like public service. Common careers include civil servant, policy analyst and public manager.

majors.name: Translation and Interpreting
majors.embedding_text: Translation and Interpreting studies how to convey meaning accurately between languages in writing and speech. It suits multilingual, precise students. Common careers include translator, interpreter and localisation specialist.

majors.name: Audiology
majors.embedding_text: Audiology studies hearing and balance and how to diagnose and treat related disorders. It suits precise, caring, science-minded students. Common careers include audiologist and hearing health specialist.

majors.name: Construction Management
majors.embedding_text: Construction Management studies how to plan, cost and deliver building projects on time and budget. It suits organised, practical students. Common careers include construction manager, project manager and quantity surveyor.

careers.name: Software Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A software engineer designs, builds and maintains computer programs and applications. They write code, fix bugs and work in teams to ship reliable software. This is one of the fastest-growing, well-paid technology careers worldwide.

careers.name: AI Engineer
careers.embedding_text: An AI engineer builds and deploys machine learning models and intelligent systems. They train models on data and integrate them into products. Demand is rising rapidly as organisations adopt artificial intelligence.

careers.name: Data Scientist
careers.embedding_text: A data scientist analyses large datasets to find patterns and build predictive models that inform decisions. They combine statistics, programming and domain knowledge. It is among the fastest-growing technical occupations.

careers.name: Data Analyst
careers.embedding_text: A data analyst collects, cleans and interprets data to answer business questions and build reports. They turn raw numbers into clear insights for decision makers. Demand is growing as organisations rely more on data.

careers.name: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.embedding_text: A cybersecurity analyst protects an organisation's systems and data from cyber attacks by monitoring threats and responding to incidents. Rising cyber threats make this one of the fastest-growing technology roles.

careers.name: Network Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A network engineer designs, builds and maintains the computer networks that connect devices and users. They keep data flowing securely and reliably. Demand grows with cloud computing and connectivity needs.

careers.name: DevOps Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A DevOps engineer automates how software is built, tested and released so teams can ship faster and more reliably. They bridge development and operations. Demand is strong as companies modernise software delivery.

careers.name: Web Developer
careers.embedding_text: A web developer builds and maintains websites and web applications, handling layout, functionality and performance. They work with languages like HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Demand grows with the digital economy.

careers.name: Database Administrator
careers.embedding_text: A database administrator designs, secures and maintains the databases that store an organisation's information. They ensure data is available, fast and safe. Demand grows with the volume of data.

careers.name: IT Support Specialist
careers.embedding_text: An IT support specialist helps users solve computer and software problems and keeps technology running. They troubleshoot issues and maintain equipment. The role is steady, with some automation of routine tasks.

careers.name: Game Developer
careers.embedding_text: A game developer designs and programs video games, building gameplay, graphics and interactive features. They combine creativity and technical skill. The games industry continues to expand.

careers.name: UX Designer
careers.embedding_text: A UX designer makes products easy and pleasant to use by researching users and designing clear interfaces. They shape how apps and websites feel. Demand grows as companies compete on user experience.

careers.name: Electrical Engineer
careers.embedding_text: An electrical engineer designs and tests electrical systems and devices, from power grids to electronics. They apply physics and mathematics to real problems. It is a stable, well-paid engineering career.

careers.name: Mechanical Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A mechanical engineer designs, builds and tests machines and mechanical systems used across industries. They turn ideas into working products. It remains a core, dependable engineering profession.

careers.name: Civil Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A civil engineer plans and oversees the construction of infrastructure such as roads, bridges and buildings. They ensure projects are safe and sound. Demand grows with infrastructure investment.

careers.name: Chemical Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A chemical engineer designs processes that turn raw materials into products like fuels, medicines and plastics. They scale chemistry to industry. The field is steady and well paid.

careers.name: Aerospace Engineer
careers.embedding_text: An aerospace engineer designs and tests aircraft, spacecraft and their systems. They work on flight, propulsion and structures. It is a specialised engineering field tied to aviation and space.

careers.name: Biomedical Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A biomedical engineer designs medical devices, imaging systems and prosthetics that improve healthcare. They combine engineering with biology and medicine. Demand grows with healthcare technology.

careers.name: Industrial Engineer
careers.embedding_text: An industrial engineer improves how organisations work by making processes more efficient and reducing waste. They optimise systems in factories, hospitals and logistics. Employment is projected to grow faster than average.

careers.name: Environmental Engineer
careers.embedding_text: An environmental engineer designs solutions to protect the environment, such as cleaning water and reducing pollution. They apply engineering to sustainability challenges. Demand grows with climate concerns.

careers.name: Robotics Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A robotics engineer designs and builds robots and automated systems for industry and research. They combine mechanics, electronics and software. Automation demand is driving strong growth.

careers.name: Petroleum Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A petroleum engineer plans and manages the extraction of oil and gas from underground reserves. They optimise drilling and production. Pay is high, though long-term growth is uncertain amid the energy transition.

careers.name: Renewable Energy Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A renewable energy engineer designs and develops clean energy systems such as solar and wind power. They help shift the world toward sustainable energy. Related occupations are among the fastest growing.

careers.name: Manufacturing Engineer
careers.embedding_text: A manufacturing engineer designs and improves the processes used to make products efficiently and reliably. They keep production lines running well. The role is steady across industry.

careers.name: Mathematician
careers.embedding_text: A mathematician uses advanced mathematics to solve problems and develop theories in research, industry and government. Demand for mathematical skills is growing with data and modelling needs.

careers.name: Statistician
careers.embedding_text: A statistician designs studies and analyses data to draw reliable conclusions under uncertainty. They work in health, government, business and research. Employment is projected to grow much faster than average.

careers.name: Actuary
careers.embedding_text: An actuary uses mathematics and statistics to measure and price risk, mainly in insurance and pensions. They protect organisations from financial uncertainty. It is a high-paid, fast-growing profession.

careers.name: Quantitative Analyst
careers.embedding_text: A quantitative analyst builds mathematical models to price assets and manage risk in financial markets. They blend maths, statistics and coding. It is a demanding, very well-paid finance role.

careers.name: Physicist
careers.embedding_text: A physicist studies matter, energy and the laws of nature through theory and experiment. They work in research, industry and technology. Skills transfer well into data and engineering roles.

careers.name: Chemist
careers.embedding_text: A chemist studies substances and their reactions to develop new materials, medicines and products. They work mostly in laboratories. The field is steady across pharma, materials and industry.

careers.name: Research Scientist
careers.embedding_text: A research scientist designs and runs experiments to advance knowledge in fields like biology, physics or computing. They publish findings and develop new methods. Demand grows in R&D-intensive sectors.

careers.name: Biologist
careers.embedding_text: A biologist studies living organisms and how they function, in the lab or the field. They contribute to medicine, conservation and biotechnology. Demand grows with health and environmental needs.

careers.name: Biochemist
careers.embedding_text: A biochemist studies the chemical processes inside living things to understand health and develop treatments. They work in labs and research. Demand grows with biotech and pharmaceuticals.

careers.name: Geneticist
careers.embedding_text: A geneticist studies genes and heredity, increasingly using genomics and large datasets. They advance medicine, agriculture and research. The field grows with genomic technology.

careers.name: Biotechnologist
careers.embedding_text: A biotechnologist uses living systems to create products in medicine, agriculture and industry. They apply biology to innovation. Demand grows with the expanding biotech sector.

careers.name: Pharmacologist
careers.embedding_text: A pharmacologist studies how drugs affect the body and helps develop and test new medicines. They work in research and pharmaceuticals. Demand grows with drug development.

careers.name: Environmental Scientist
careers.embedding_text: An environmental scientist studies the natural world and human impact on it to protect ecosystems and health. They collect data and advise on sustainability. Demand grows with climate concern.

careers.name: Geologist
careers.embedding_text: A geologist studies the Earth's materials, structure and history, including natural resources and hazards. They combine fieldwork and analysis. Demand follows resources, energy and environment.

careers.name: Astronomer
careers.embedding_text: An astronomer studies stars, planets and the universe using physics, mathematics and large datasets. They work mostly in research and academia. Positions are limited but skills transfer to data science.

careers.name: Doctor
careers.embedding_text: A doctor diagnoses and treats illness and injury and cares for patients' health. They work in clinics and hospitals after long training. Demand grows with an ageing population.

careers.name: Surgeon
careers.embedding_text: A surgeon performs operations to treat injury, disease and deformity. They combine medical knowledge with precise manual skill. It is a highly paid, demanding medical career.

careers.name: Nurse
careers.embedding_text: A nurse cares for patients, administers treatments and supports recovery in hospitals and the community. They are central to healthcare teams. Demand is strong and growing with healthcare needs.

careers.name: Nurse Practitioner
careers.embedding_text: A nurse practitioner is an advanced nurse who can diagnose, treat and prescribe, often as a primary care provider. They expand access to care. It is among the fastest-growing healthcare occupations.

careers.name: Dentist
careers.embedding_text: A dentist diagnoses and treats problems with teeth and gums and promotes oral health. They run clinics and perform procedures. It is a stable, well-paid healthcare profession.

careers.name: Pharmacist
careers.embedding_text: A pharmacist prepares and dispenses medicines and advises patients on their safe use. They work in pharmacies, hospitals and industry. The role is steady with growing clinical responsibilities.

careers.name: Physiotherapist
careers.embedding_text: A physiotherapist helps people recover movement and manage pain after injury or illness. They use exercise and physical treatment. Demand is growing fast with an ageing population.

careers.name: Veterinarian
careers.embedding_text: A veterinarian diagnoses and treats illness and injury in animals and advises owners on care. They run clinics and perform surgery. Pet-care demand is driving fast growth.

careers.name: Psychologist
careers.embedding_text: A psychologist studies behaviour and helps people with mental health and wellbeing through assessment and therapy. They work in clinics, schools and organisations. Demand grows with mental health awareness.

careers.name: Psychiatrist
careers.embedding_text: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who diagnoses and treats mental illness, including prescribing medication. They support people with complex conditions. Demand grows with mental health needs.

careers.name: Dietitian
careers.embedding_text: A dietitian advises people on healthy eating and uses nutrition to manage and prevent illness. They work in clinics, communities and industry. Demand grows with focus on health and prevention.

careers.name: Occupational Therapist
careers.embedding_text: An occupational therapist helps people regain independence in everyday activities after injury, illness or disability. They adapt tasks and environments. Demand is growing quickly in healthcare.

careers.name: Speech Therapist
careers.embedding_text: A speech therapist helps people with communication and swallowing difficulties of all ages. They assess and deliver therapy. Demand is growing fast across health and education.

careers.name: Midwife
careers.embedding_text: A midwife supports women through pregnancy, birth and the early days of parenthood. They provide clinical care and reassurance. Demand remains steady to growing in maternal health.

careers.name: Optometrist
careers.embedding_text: An optometrist examines eyes, tests vision and prescribes corrective lenses, and detects eye disease. They run practices and clinics. Demand grows with an ageing population.

careers.name: Medical Laboratory Scientist
careers.embedding_text: A medical laboratory scientist runs tests on samples to help diagnose and monitor disease. They are essential to clinical decisions. Demand grows with healthcare and diagnostics.

careers.name: Radiographer
careers.embedding_text: A radiographer produces medical images such as X-rays and scans to help diagnose illness and injury. They operate imaging equipment and care for patients. Demand grows with diagnostic imaging.

careers.name: Public Health Specialist
careers.embedding_text: A public health specialist works to protect and improve the health of whole populations through prevention, data and policy. They track disease and design programmes. Demand grows with health challenges.

careers.name: Economist
careers.embedding_text: An economist studies how resources are produced and used and advises on policy and strategy. They analyse data and forecast trends. Demand is steady in government, finance and consulting.

careers.name: Financial Analyst
careers.embedding_text: A financial analyst evaluates investments, companies and markets to guide financial decisions. They build models and write recommendations. Demand grows with finance and investment activity.

careers.name: Investment Banker
careers.embedding_text: An investment banker helps companies raise money and complete mergers and acquisitions. They advise on large financial deals. Pay is high; demand fluctuates with markets.

careers.name: Accountant
careers.embedding_text: An accountant prepares and examines financial records and ensures they are accurate and lawful. They support individuals and businesses. Employment is projected to grow faster than average.

careers.name: Financial Advisor
careers.embedding_text: A financial advisor helps people manage money, invest and plan for goals like retirement. They build long-term client relationships. An ageing population drives strong demand.

careers.name: Management Consultant
careers.embedding_text: A management consultant advises organisations on how to solve problems and improve performance. They analyse issues and recommend change. Demand stays strong in professional services.

careers.name: Business Analyst
careers.embedding_text: A business analyst studies how a business works and recommends improvements, often involving technology and data. They bridge business and IT. Demand grows with digital transformation.

careers.name: Project Manager
careers.embedding_text: A project manager plans and delivers projects on time and budget by coordinating people and resources. They manage scope and risk. Demand stays strong across industries.

careers.name: Product Manager
careers.embedding_text: A product manager decides what a product should do and guides its development from idea to launch. They balance users, business and technology. Demand is strong in tech and beyond.

careers.name: Marketing Manager
careers.embedding_text: A marketing manager plans and runs campaigns to promote products and build brands. They lead teams and budgets. Demand stays steady with a shift toward digital marketing.

careers.name: Digital Marketer
careers.embedding_text: A digital marketer promotes products online through search, social media and advertising. They use data to improve results. Demand grows as marketing moves online.

careers.name: Human Resources Manager
careers.embedding_text: A human resources manager recruits, develops and supports an organisation's people and handles workplace issues. They shape culture and policy. Demand stays steady across sectors.

careers.name: Supply Chain Manager
careers.embedding_text: A supply chain manager oversees how goods and materials move from suppliers to customers efficiently. They manage logistics and procurement. Demand grows with global trade and e-commerce.

careers.name: Entrepreneur
careers.embedding_text: An entrepreneur starts and grows their own business, taking on risk to turn an idea into a venture. They lead in uncertainty. Outcomes vary widely, from modest to highly successful.

careers.name: Lawyer
careers.embedding_text: A lawyer advises and represents clients on legal matters and in disputes. They interpret law and argue cases. It is a well-paid profession with steady demand.

careers.name: Paralegal
careers.embedding_text: A paralegal supports lawyers by researching cases, preparing documents and organising files. They are vital to legal teams. Demand grows as firms seek efficiency.

careers.name: Policy Analyst
careers.embedding_text: A policy analyst researches issues and advises governments and organisations on policy choices. They weigh evidence and trade-offs. Demand stays steady in public and non-profit sectors.

careers.name: Diplomat
careers.embedding_text: A diplomat represents their country abroad, building relationships and negotiating on its behalf. They work in embassies and international organisations. Entry is competitive.

careers.name: Civil Servant
careers.embedding_text: A civil servant helps run government and deliver public services and policy. They work across departments and agencies. The role is stable and varied.

careers.name: Teacher
careers.embedding_text: A teacher educates students and supports their development in schools. They plan lessons and assess progress. Demand is steady, varying by subject and region.

careers.name: University Lecturer
careers.embedding_text: A university lecturer teaches and conducts research in higher education. They share expertise and advance knowledge. Academic positions are competitive but stable.

careers.name: Architect
careers.embedding_text: An architect designs buildings and spaces that are safe, functional and attractive. They turn ideas into detailed plans. Demand follows construction and development.

careers.name: Urban Planner
careers.embedding_text: An urban planner shapes how towns and cities develop, balancing housing, transport and the environment. They guide land use and policy. Demand grows with urbanisation.

careers.name: Surveyor
careers.embedding_text: A surveyor measures and assesses land, property and construction costs. They provide data that guides building and development. The role is steady in construction and property.

careers.name: Construction Manager
careers.embedding_text: A construction manager plans and oversees building projects, coordinating workers, schedules and budgets. They keep sites safe and on track. Demand follows construction activity.

careers.name: Graphic Designer
careers.embedding_text: A graphic designer creates visual content such as logos, layouts and digital graphics to communicate messages. They blend creativity and software skills. Demand is steady with a shift to digital.

careers.name: Journalist
careers.embedding_text: A journalist researches, writes and reports news and stories across print, broadcast and online media. They inform the public. The field is competitive and changing with digital media.

careers.name: Content Writer
careers.embedding_text: A content writer creates articles, marketing copy and other written material for websites and brands. They write to inform and persuade. Demand grows with digital content needs.

careers.name: Public Relations Specialist
careers.embedding_text: A public relations specialist manages how an organisation is seen by the public and the media. They craft messages and handle communications. Demand stays steady with reputation management.

careers.name: Translator
careers.embedding_text: A translator converts written text, or an interpreter spoken words, between languages accurately. They enable cross-language communication. Demand grows with globalisation, though tools assist the work.

careers.name: Social Worker
careers.embedding_text: A social worker supports vulnerable people and families and connects them to help and services. They handle difficult situations with care. Demand is growing across community services.

careers.name: Counselor
careers.embedding_text: A counselor helps people work through emotional, mental health and life challenges through talking therapy. They provide a supportive, confidential space. Demand is growing fast with mental health needs.

careers.name: Sales Manager
careers.embedding_text: A sales manager leads a team to sell products or services and meet targets. They set strategy and motivate staff. The role is steady, though some sales tasks face automation.

careers.name: Logistics Coordinator
careers.embedding_text: A logistics coordinator organises the movement and storage of goods and keeps deliveries on schedule. They solve day-to-day supply problems. Demand grows with e-commerce and trade.

careers.name: Pilot
careers.embedding_text: A pilot flies aircraft safely to transport passengers or cargo. They manage navigation, systems and safety. Demand grows with air travel, after demanding training.

careers.name: Electrician
careers.embedding_text: An electrician installs and maintains electrical systems in homes, businesses and industry. They work hands-on and follow safety codes. Demand is growing faster than average, boosted by clean energy.

careers.name: Bioinformatician
careers.embedding_text: A bioinformatician analyses biological data such as genomes using computing and statistics. They work at the meeting point of biology and data science. Demand is growing fast in research and health.

careers.name: Sustainability Consultant
careers.embedding_text: A sustainability consultant advises organisations on reducing environmental impact and meeting climate and ESG goals. They turn sustainability into strategy. Demand is growing fast with climate priorities.

careers.name: Chef
careers.embedding_text: A chef prepares food and runs kitchens, creating menus and leading kitchen teams. They combine creativity and craft under pressure. Demand grows in hospitality and food services.

careers.name: Hotel Manager
careers.embedding_text: A hotel manager oversees the running of a hotel, ensuring good service and smooth operations. They manage staff, guests and budgets. Demand follows tourism and hospitality.

careers.name: Marine Biologist
careers.embedding_text: A marine biologist studies life in oceans and seas and works to conserve it. They combine fieldwork, lab work and analysis. Positions are competitive but tied to growing environmental interest.

careers.name: Agricultural Scientist
careers.embedding_text: An agricultural scientist works to improve crops, soil and farming methods for productive, sustainable food production. They apply science to agriculture. Demand grows with food and sustainability needs.

careers.name: Food Scientist
careers.embedding_text: A food scientist studies the chemistry and safety of food and develops new products and processes. They ensure food is safe and appealing. Demand is steady to growing in the food industry.
